newsitem.title: NAMIBIA: U.S. FIRMS INVEST N$33MLN IN NAMIBIA VEHICLE PLANT.
newsitem.headline: U.S. FIRMS INVEST N$33MLN IN NAMIBIA VEHICLE PLANT.

text.p: U.S. firms General Motors Corp and Barden International on Thursday announced a N$33 million investment in a Namibian vehicle assembly plant.
The investment is the largest ever by U.S. companies since Namibian independence in 1990.

Barden International chairman Don Barden said at a ceremony in Windhoek 70 Namibians would be employed at the upfit and processing plant for Chevrolet, Chevitruck and Cadillac vehicles, the first of which are expected to be assembled by mid-1997.

"In the final analysis this is about economic empowerment for individual Namibians and therefore we want them to be trained to be able to run and operate this facility as well as other plants and business activities that we plan to undertake in this country," Barden said.
The plant will be situated in the industrial area surrounding the capital, Windhoek.
He said the group had chosen Namibia because of its political stability, its infrastructure and its accessibility to other countries in the region.

"I made a very conscious decision not to go to South Africa because I think (factors such as) the stability, the organisation of the government and the infrastructure are much more conducive to immediate success than all the complexities in South Africa and its adjustments to democracy."
Namibia would act as the southern African headquarter of Barden International.
The company, in conjunction with the U.S. government, would offer employees training in executive management and automotive technology at the University of Michigan and Delta College in the U.S.
At the ceremony, Namibian president Sam Nujoma hailed the investment as a major success in Namibia's drive to attract foreign investment.
